claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known municipal permitting assistant performance gap and unresolved disclosure/materiality review.

concern_ledger.concern: Materiality appears triggered because the underperforming municipal permitting assistant segment is a named launch use case in two city pilot commitments.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible proof that the limitation was disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: If the limitation is material, policy requires disclosure unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No such closing evidence is in the record.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final legal determination or equivalent admissible approval resolving the disclosure requirement.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Pending legal review leaves a required policy predicate unresolved; compliance cannot be treated as established while that question is unanswered.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies on aggregate readiness and public guidance to support certification without showing the required internal support link.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence tying certification to satisfaction of the internal disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for this specific gap.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Aggregate pass and public model-governance guidance do not establish compliance with the internal rule for material limitations in named launch use cases.

concern_ledger.concern: The 'non-core' characterization does not resolve materiality for a named customer commitment.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence showing the segment is not a named launch use case or that commitments were changed, plus final legal/policy resolution.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy text expressly says product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in commitments or legal review is pending.

decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the release policy for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
General aggregate readiness evidence cannot substitute for satisfaction of a specific disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
Named customer commitments and pending legal review weigh toward materiality under the stated policy text.
Public governance guidance may support documentation and monitoring practices, but it does not by itself authorize launch contrary to internal policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Produce admissible evidence that the municipal permitting assistant gap was disclosed in the model card or other required launch documentation before launch.
Produce an approved risk acceptance covering this specific named launch use case limitation, if one exists.
Produce final legal determination on whether the gap is a material limitation requiring disclosure.
Produce admissible evidence that the performance gap was resolved to target before launch, if that is the basis for certification.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not resolve the separate policy question of whether a material limitation in a named launch use case must be disclosed before launch.
The affected municipal permitting assistant segment misses target and is named in two city pilot commitments, which fits the policy text's materiality trigger for named launch use cases.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved before launch, disclosed, or covered by an approved risk acceptance, which the policy note requires for material limitations.
Product's 'non-core' framing is weakened by the evidence that the same segment is named in customer commitments.
unsupported_claims: The actor's broader justification that certification is supported because limitations can be managed through model-card documentation and deployment monitoring overreaches the admissible evidence; the public guidance cited is general and does not override the internal disclosure policy or establish that certification without disclosure is compliant.
Any implication that the named segment gap is immaterial is unsupported because admissible evidence ties that segment to two city pilot commitments and notes pending legal review.
